overview.headline: Radioactive decay provides numeric ages for the geologic time scale

keyPoints.point: The assignment of rock ages in thousands, millions, and billions of years was made possible by the discovery of radioactivity
keyPoints.quote: The assignment of ages of rocks in thousands, millions, and billions of years was made possible by the discovery of radioactivity.

keyPoints.point: The half-life of a radioactive isotope is the length of time for one-half of parent atoms to decay to daughter atoms
keyPoints.quote: The half-life of a radioactive isotope is the length of time required for exactly one-half of the parent atoms to decay to daughter atoms.

keyPoints.point: four parent/daughter decay series are especially useful for dating and include carbon to nitrogen and potassium to argon
keyPoints.quote: four parent/daughter decay series are especially useful: carbon to nitrogen, potassium to argon, rubidium to strontium, and uranium to lead.

keyPoints.point: Isotopic techniques are used to measure the time at which a particular mineral within a rock was formed
keyPoints.quote: Isotopic techniques are used to measure the time at which a particular mineral within a rock was formed.
